title: add JSONSchema structured output: strict mode + OpenAI compatibility
author: Samir Patel
body:
Motivation: Add first-class JSONSchema-based structured output support to the Redwood API surface, including a strict validation mode and improved error messages. This brings our response_format schema features closer to OpenAI compatibility while giving explicit controls for strictness and structured error payloads.

This PR: 1) Introduces response_format: {type: 'json_schema', schema_id: '...', strict: true|false} handling in the API layer; 2) Implements server-side schema validation with deterministic error payloads and diagnostics; 3) Adds an OpenAI-compatibility flag to return errors and nulls in formats clients expect; 4) Improves streaming stability when schema validation is enabled by deferring final validation to the end-of-stream while providing early warnings in the stream; 5) Adds exhaustive unit and integration tests and docs.

Checklist:
- [x] API surface for response_format JSON schema and strict flag
- [x] Validation engine (jsonschema + Redwood-specific extensions)
- [x] Streaming behavior: early warnings + final validation enforcement
- [x] OpenAI compatibility mode for error payloads and null handling
- [x] Tests: unit, integration, e2e with examples
- [x] Docs and release notes

Compatibility notes: Default behavior remains backward-compatible: response_format omitted yields existing behavior. When strict=true, invalid outputs will cause the request to fail with a structured error. When openai_compat=true, error payloads follow OpenAI error shape and invalid fields are returned as nulls in the final parsed object where applicable.

Implementation details: Validation is performed post-generation against the provided JSONSchema. To avoid large latency regressions we: 1) run a lightweight schema conformance check during token generation to provide early warnings on the stream (non-blocking); 2) perform full validation at end-of-stream and return a structured validation error if strict=true; 3) in openai_compat mode, we map validation failures to the OpenAI-style error object and optionally patch missing fields to null where the schema allows.

Testing & rollout: Added unit tests around the validation engine and streaming integration tests that simulate partial outputs and streaming early-warning metadata. CI flakiness observed on first run (one flaky test in streaming harness) was fixed by making the test harness deterministic. Will feature-flag rollout for 2 weeks before enabling strict mode by default for new models.

Related: linear/ENG-10234, PM-4561 for product acceptance criteria.
commits: feat(api): add response_format json_schema parsing and validation registration
feat(runtime): wire validation into streaming pipeline (early-warning metadata)
feat(compat): add openai_compat mappings for schema errors and null coalescing
test: add unit tests for schema validator and streaming integration
docs: document response_format json_schema and strict/openai_compat flags
fix(test): stabilize streaming harness timing to avoid flaky assertions
review_comments: Arianna Kim: Nice end-to-end. Can you clarify how this interacts with existing prefix caching? We don't want cache poisoning.
Samir Patel (author): Good catch — validator checks include an opaque cache key that only enables caching when response_format is absent or explicitly cacheable. Added comment and unit test.
Diego Morales: Prefer making openai_compat opt-in (not default). Also please include example of the OpenAI error payload in docs.
Samir Patel (author): openai_compat is opt-in. Docs updated with example payloads and mapping table.
Lena Fischer: CI initially failed due to flakey streaming test; post-fix run looks clean. Approving after tests pass.
Arianna Kim: Approve — ergonomics look good and rollback plan clear.
release_notes: Added JSONSchema-based structured output support with a strict validation mode and OpenAI-compatible error mapping. Enables deterministic validation errors and streaming early-warning metadata. Feature gated; strict mode must be enabled per-request. See docs/api/response_format.md for examples and migration notes.
